There is nothing here like two periods or time interval or anything that would diminish the correctness of these two samples and the possibility to cross-reference them and compare it. There is the overlap in the last row of this table which tells 1.039 cases were reported involve samples. So what Mr. Karadzic just told us about period of drawing the samples does not apply to this situation at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 1700 is a number of deaths that can be found in household survey?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And 1500 is number found in Bakije?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And there is an overlap of 1.000 numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In that case, total number of deaths is 2.5 million?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, 2500.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what we obtained too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, back to you, Mr. Karadzic. Thank you, Ms. West and Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain the first figure of 1.707. Does it also include Christian households, both Serbian and Croatian?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sarajevo household survey included all people who lived within the front lines. So obviously all ethnicities that were there are in the survey records.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you say that Bakijes buried Christians?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not, it is a Muslim funeral home. But for this reason the whole capture/recapture started by taking Muslims from both sources, so extracting relevant records from household survey Sarajevo as to end exclusively with the Muslims and same with the Bakije funeral home. I want to mention ethnicity comes from the 1991 population census, from the links with the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that in Sarajevo there is a funeral parlor which only deals with atheists, i.e., there's only atheists of all religions and ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be so, but I didn't look for this and I didn't use this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us say that the Bakije funeral parlor had a good record of all the bodies that they buried. What about the Muslims that were not buried by the Bakije funeral home? Is there comparable grounds or grounds to compare because there is a list of households, the second list is of the bodies that the Bakije funeral home buried, the third would be a list of persons buried by other funeral homes? How do you make your calculations from that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We rather opted for using two sources of which we knew were very well suited for these type of analysis. Bakije is the largest funeral home in Sarajevo with a long history and burying Muslims. It is a very good source for this kind of analysis. So what we have done we have completed the estimation for the Muslims and then extrapolated this result over the other ethnic groups which is a very justified assumption because we don't discuss here in the case of Sarajevo a case of ethnic cleansing. So there is a very good reason to assume that the same extrapolation can be done for other ethnicities as what we produced for Muslims from capture/recapture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your opinion is this formula applied to valid or invalid variables?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course it is in the case how we did it is applied to valid variables, valid samples; otherwise, why would I be presenting it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In my understanding a sample is one thing and a variable is another. Is this applied to valid or invalid variables?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then perhaps you tell me first what is a variable you are talking about and what is your definition of validity of this variable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll deal with that when the time comes. Tell me, does this include any coefficient pertaining to age, average age of the population? Were death rates taken into account? Could you apply any of that to this formula?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you are talking about, but I can tell that in the capture/recapture estimation we didn't use any age distribution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I supposed to understand this in the following way, that this is not longitudinal, that it is not diachronic, and that it has nothing to do with time? Is that right? What does that mean that at one point in time there were 1700 and as far as Bakije is concerned, 1500. Which period are you referring to? What are the dynamics involved? What was it that you inferred on that basis?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned the time-frame for this estimation earlier today. It is as in the title of the table A6.1. It is the period from 1st of April, 1992, to 9 September 1992. That is the time-frame for the number, the estimated number produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that perhaps this method could be used by a bird institute or in the case of human beings an institute for demographic research? Do you believe that this kind of method would be applicable in matters related to criminal law?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually I can tell you with certainty that capture/recapture and several other methods related to capture/recapture is one of the major methods for estimation of unknown numbers of victims of war. It has been used in several other areas of study and there is a whole area of application called multiple system estimation where the number of samples goes beyond three and simple formulas like this one cannot be easily proposed. So there is a log linear modeling analysis that was applied for this kind of study. So I think capture/recapture is the way to go when it comes to unknown numbers of, among others, victims of war. This method has also been applied many times in epidemiology for estimation of HIV patients, for instance, or for drug addicts that are also a category that is very hard to measure and several other phenomena that cannot be directly observed and measures. So actually, what we have been doing here is very much in line with a broader field of analysis related to unknown population sizes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you testified in any other court of law apart from this one, and you testified here 17 times. Did you testify anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Except for epidemiological or demographic studies that do not have criminal law applications, has this method been applied anywhere else? Has it been accepted in legal practice, as it were?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell whether this method has been accepted in legal practice related to epidemiology or other areas. I think -- I wouldn't think that in other international criminal tribunals a similar type of result were produced and tendered in evidence in other cases. What we've been doing in this Tribunal is actually unique, I must say. On the other hand, other tribunals, like for instance the Khmer Rouge trial in Phnom Penh, are in a much more difficult position because sources that are available for the estimation of war victims are not available to the same extent as it is the case in the former Yugoslavia. From this point of view the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina is a very exceptional case. There is a lot of information, high quality often information that can be used to propose this kind of measures like counts of victims and estimated more complete numbers. It is a very unique situation, I think, [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're coming to the objective. The objective of this research of yours primarily dealt with Muslims, right, the percentage of the Muslim population and displaced persons, refugees, and so on; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not right. I think all ethnic groups were included in my reports, especially in the municipality reports in which measures of population displacement are presented, all ethnic groups are included. The same is with Sarajevo, all ethnic groups are included and the same is with Srebrenica. Only in the case of Srebrenica it happens that almost all victim were of Muslim ethnicity and were men. So this is a result but has nothing to do with our approach when it comes to ethnicity. I think in all the reports every ethnic group is represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to that. So what was the objective? Can you tell us briefly what the objective was and also can you tell us whether you attained that objective.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the objectives of course were different in all these reports. In the municipalities report the objective was to measure the displacement of the population, the displacement related to the war in these territories. Displacement in terms of both internal displacement and external displacement. In Sarajevo reports the objective was to quantify the number of victims of the siege and analyse basic distributions of these victims. The objective was as well to propose estimates that could be used to assess the degree of incompleteness of the minimum numbers that were produced from our sources. Finally, in the Srebrenica reports the objectives are also different. Srebrenica is a very special case. We study a particular group of victims, the missing persons, of whom we have very good reasons to believe that they were killed, they didn't die natural deaths as their bodies are often exhumed from mass graves and other graves. So the objective was to check, to investigate, how many of them were there related to the fall of Srebrenica and how much we know about the fate 15 years after the war ended. And obviously in the course of time we have learned a great deal about the fate of these people, as today after 15 years we can say 81.1 per cent of all the missing persons have been identified. We know the DNA profile. We know where the bodies were. Families of many of them were able to bury them in their own graves, family graves, so that that were the objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you've given such an extensive answer let us try to complete one thing with regard to the things that you talked about today. These 116 persons were added subsequently, like the 200-something who survived. Were they at one point in time an integral part of the list of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The whole point is, as I discussed this several times today, sources on war victims overlap and largely so, but there are also unique parts of these sources that bring new information to the general picture of victimisation. The new cases, 116, 213, are the unique records from the ICMP from DNA identification process of victims of Srebrenica. For this reason they are reported as new and additional cases because we couldn't confirm we couldn't find them in ICRC records.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the persons who are now considered to be survivors, were they ever part of the statistical mass of persons who were considered to be missing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At some point early in time they were, but the purpose of our investigation of cross-referencing our list with sources on survivors is to exclude such cases. So in the course of time we were able to confirm them as, for instance, records of refugees or displaced persons. This is the reason that tells us something is wrong here and this is why we have these 12 exclusions from our records.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What's the total number of survivors found in this entire mass of almost 8.000 persons who are recorded as missing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the 12 records that are listed in the table, so that is the entire mass of possible survivors. So the thing is that, you know, if you work with records of missing persons, the hope that the person at some point will be found alive is really very, very small. So it is -- for missing persons what we see is as a general rule almost, these persons are found in the mass graves, other graves exhumed and identified. It is for Srebrenica on the first place but also for other episodes of war. So as I'm saying missing persons is a very, very special category of victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now say that the process of establishing the number of survivors has been completed or can new survivors still be discovered?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that what could be done has been done, but every time when there are new victims, like the 116 or 213, for these new records a search is always done and a comparison of these records with sources on survivors, in order to see whether possibly for these new cases there is an overlap with sources on survivors or not. But because these new records are coming from ICMP, that is, a source reporting on DNA identifications of victims, again the chance that they would be found on survivors lists is nil, simply not possible. Sometimes it might happen that the record of such a victim will be seen in the record of refugees or displaced persons, but then it is very likely that a mistake is in the survivor record. It happens sometimes and it can be clarified by questioning the family of such a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your opinion, who reported missing persons for the most part or in most cases or exclusively, if you will? Actually, who could have reported that a certain person was missing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: ICRC, that is, the source that we used for the list of missing from Srebrenica, have always been extremely selective when it comes to the respondents. The only accepted reports on a missing person from the family of this person, it is just the standard way they operate. It is not possible for them to accept any report of going missing. In order to produce a very reliable list of missing persons they have to follow very strict procedures about how to collect this information, and this is what they do. So respondents must be the family of a victim. Further information must be relatively detailed. So it's impossible to drop just a name and that's it. People have to be more specific about it. ICRC uses a standardised questionnaire to collect answers from their respondents. So there is a lot of attention paid by the ICRC when collecting the data.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd kindly ask you to try to be as belief as possible. I'll try to put questions that can be answered by a mere yes or no. Was a mechanism established involving some obligation on the part of a person who reported someone missing, did that person then have to say if that person was found that the person was no longer missing?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unaware of a mechanism that ICRC put in place. It was, I believe, up to the families to go back to the ICRC and tell them whether or not this person was confirmed alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there a mechanism, or rather, is there an obligation on the part of the family to do that every now and then, to say that a person remains missing or to say that a person reappeared in the meantime. Or rather, to be more specific, once a person is reported as missing for the first time, is there any established mechanism and obligation on the part of the person who reported that to update the information provided?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that probably there is no such obligation to the respondents. However, ICRC co-operates closely with ICMP. They exchange information. And ICRC, as far as I know, is also updated by ICMP about their identifications. By again comparing the lists, ICRC can categorise the missing persons into still missing persons, missing persons with a known place of death, missing persons dead, closed cases, and exclusions. This is actually how the ICRC provided us with their lists in 2005 and recently, more recently, in 2008. So I would think there is an effort, systematic effort at ICRC to update the information they have. On the web, for instance, only records of still missing persons are included, not all the records, not the closed cases, but just still missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I cannot give you an exact page reference now, but I'm sure that you're going to recognise this assertion of yours. When you say that the reliability of sources is rather satisfactory but not comparable to usual statistical sources, what did you mean by that? Would it have been better had you had the usual statistical sources?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The usual statistical sources that I used, by the way, in my work as well, this is the 1991 population census that we used. We also used DEM-2 mortality databases that were compiled by professional statisticians. DEM-2 mortality databases were those used for the Dragomir Milosevic report. Well, what is different when a statistical authority compiles a source, these are people who are trained to do this work. They know about how to collect information, how to develop questionnaires to be used in surveys, how to process this information. They know about cleaning the data. They know about elimination about duplicates and about cases that are incomplete. So if a statistical authority makes a source, obviously the quality of information is better. However, ICRC, not being a professional statistical authority, in my view, has done a lot of effort to produce reliable information. And as far as I can compare, you know, ICRC versus other sources that I have been using, I can tell that ICRC is a reliable source of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that it would be a good thing if two phenomena were to be compared from identical sources. To be more specific, for example, you compared the 1991 census and the voters register from 1997 and 1998. Are they the same kind of sources?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not because voters register is just a source made for different purposes. However, in the case of Bosnia in 1997 and 1998 election, voters register is nothing else but a subset of the census data. Actually, the requirement for a voter to register to vote was that the voter had to be enlisted in the -- on the 1991 census on the first place. So from this point of view for the purposes of my work here, I mean the municipalities report, the voters register is a very good source to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask you to give me answers that are as brief as possible. Was the census compulsory? Did a citizen have to be registered in 1991?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: All persons living in Bosnia had to participate in the 1991 census.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about voting, did a citizen have to vote? Did a citizen have to apply to vote?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, it is a voluntarily process, the registration to vote. So the answer is no, not everybody had to vote, only those who wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the elections in 1996 were closer to the events of 1991 through 1995 than was the case in 1997 and 1998? Also, thereby they would have been a more accurate indicator?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were closer in time, but not more accurate. The 1996 election is reported by OSCE in their reports as being characterised by cases of fraud and misusing the voter's name to acquire majority in certain municipalities. Secondly, it is also reported that for this particular election, 1996 election, that the list of eligible voters contained mistakes. It was sorted, not according moreover -- not according to the JMBG but other characteristics. And it was extremely difficult for the voters to find their name on this list. So in effect of this procedure, very deficient procedure, many thousand of voters were unable to vote and participate in the elections. So there are very good reasons for not using the 1996 voters register, and instead to use 1997/1998 which are known of being very good high quality with a very high participation rate of 88 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the OSCE was in charge of these elections as well, so are you trying to say that in 1997 and 1998 there were more voters than in 1996? That would be less favourable for those who are championing genocide.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we -- so the 1996 election register could not be used for very good reasons. So we had to use 1997/1998. Whether the numbers produced would be better from the 1996 voters' register, I don't think so. If you think about the process of returns then you can easily imagine that between 1996 and 1997 some people must have returned to their homes. So this only means that they are not listed in our statistics as displaced persons. So if you think how conservative or not conservative our statistics based on the 1997 voters' register are, I am telling they are more conservative because of the returns process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But why did you decide on that? Why didn't you carry out an analysis including 1996 and then leave it up to the Chamber to decide? Who made a decision to exclude the 1996 election data?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the decision was made in the demographic unit here in the Tribunal and we in co-operation with the OSCE who actually provided us with the voters' records. And I think my role is not to propose and make analysis that by definition are wrong and biassed. Instead, my objective is to make and present analyses that are reliable and meaningful. So using the 1996 voters' register is not consistent with this objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: However, as a matter of fact, were there more voters in 1996 election than in 1997 and 1998 election?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think there were more because many were unable to register. And moreover, there were cases, and frequently so, of fraud, that voters registered for certain municipalities and they shouldn't. There were like duplicate registrations which inflated the numbers in the register. So these are serious biases and, well, it's not a good source to be used in this kind of analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In answering the question because the Chamber does not know which numbers so it's very difficult to follow. So in terms of result 1996 election has more voters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I can check the number to tell whether more or not. Disregarding the number, the problem is that there is a bias in the voters register. So if people registered for certain municipalities and were not entitled to, how can I distinguish between those who were entitled and those who were not but committed an act of fraud. And also I see it is unable to pin point and flag these kind of cases. So this is very deficient source. This is what I am saying.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the interpreters are perplexed as well because we didn't receive the interpretation of the last answer, but I would kindly ask the Chamber to arrange for the voters' register from 1996 to be provided to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for the Chamber to intervene at the moment. Consult your legal advisor. We'll take a break for half an hour and resume at 3.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, when it comes to OSCE, did it annul the 1996 elections and did it issue an official report to the effect that the elections were irregular?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I have a complete translation, but just to double-check. The question is who made this report, what organisation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I will repeat. We're talking about OSCE, did it declare the elections irregular or did it at least issue an official report? I'm talking about the 1996 elections that were carried out under the supervision of the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they made their report in which they summarised problems around the 1996 elections. So what I'm saying about problems is coming from that report. There were problems related to the fact that voters could choose for any given municipality, disregarding where they lived before the war in 1991. So there was no close -- no procedure in the election registration that was checking the place of residence in 1991. It was possible to register for any municipality, and people were abusing this situation. This is discussed in this OSCE report related to activities in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1996 and in which there is a separate long chapter about problems around 1996 elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you ask me, there are always problems with elections in the Balkans. Were the elections declared null and void? Did OSCE declare the elections irregular and renounce them as such?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of a statement, official statement, that would be declaring these elections completely invalid, but -- well, I would have to double-check if it was the case. As of now, I am unaware of such a declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would appreciate it very much if you would prepare for tomorrow information as to whether people voted even from America and elsewhere, if ballots indeed arrived in sacks full of ballots. Did people vote wherever they wanted to vote or did they only vote in the municipalities where they were registered in 1991? In any case, I'm sure that you were informed and do you think that the 1997 elections were general elections for municipal authorities across Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that were municipal elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if I put it to you that the 1997 elections were only for the parliament of Republika Srpska after Mrs. Plavsic walked away from the SDS and decided that there would be a snap election for the parliament of Republika Srpska, did you know that? Were you informed about that? Did you check that if you were informed about that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be so that that was the case. What I know is that mainly these elections, 1997, were for municipal parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In all of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the entire Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm afraid that that wasn't the case. Do you know that the snap election happened after arguments among the Serbs and that Muslims were not too keen to vote in that election, therefore they didn't register at all?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to comment on the snap elections because I didn't study it in particular. But from what I can see from the register that I received from OSCE for the 1997 election, it is a complete register in the sense that the entire country is covered, both Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and all ethnic groups are represented there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Muslims and all Muslim parties in 1996 election of 83 MPs in the Assembly of Republika Srpska won 18 places, and a year later only 14 places?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of these numbers and I didn't study the results of elections, you know, especially in 1996. I don't know that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But that directly points to the fact that the 1997 list of voters was much shorter in the Muslim segment than it was in 1996 because if you had to have about 18- to 20.000 people per MP, four MPs less represents about 55.000 to 60.000 Muslim voters who did not vote for their own MPs in that year.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, what I can tell you about the 1997 voters' register, it comprises 2.5 million individuals from the entire country, and I wasn't particularly interested in the municipalities they voted for. I was interested in the municipality where they registered to vote. So it is the physical location of the registration to vote that interested me. Why? Because I took it as a good approximation of the place of residence at the time of 1997 elections. So how they voted, for what municipalities, it really didn't interest me at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what if they did not register or if fewer of them registered in 1997 than in 1996, would that have -- be significant for your research because a register or a list of voters is your second bench-mark value with regard to the 1991 census that was compulsory?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If they did not register to vote, they were not included in my study. I only studied those who registered to vote, and there were 2.5 million of registered voters in 1997 elections. That is one thing. If you said -- if there were fewer of them registered in 1997 compared to 1996, what kind of problem it creates for me? It doesn't create any problem at all because, as I said, 1997 gives more conservative numbers of displaced persons than 1996, more conservative meaning smaller, lowered numbers, more conservative numbers of displaced persons. And speaking of 1997 election and voters' register versus the 1991 population census, yes, you are right. Population census is complete. It is not a sample. It is a complete record of the population at the outbreak of the conflict. 1997 voters' register is a sample of this population. It's a very large sample, 2.5 million individuals out of initially 4.4 million in 1991. It is such a large sample that in statistical terms this is huge, it is massive. It is much, much, much more than what I need to produce reliable statistics. In my report I produced minimum numbers, minimum numbers. This is at least numbers not complete numbers. Complete numbers are higher than what are presented as the minimum from the sample, from the actually observed data.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Two and a half million adults who had the right to vote in respect of 4 million and 400.000, this obviously surpasses the customary rate of minors by far, does it not, of those who do not have the voting right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you are saying population of age 0 up to 17 versus 18 or older - just double-checking that this is what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The 18-plus population, it's much larger than 0 to 17, the minors, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the specific rate, or rather, what is the natality in Bosnia and Herzegovina per 1.000 inhabitants? You did take that into account, did you not, when you tried to establish the number of those who were born before 1980?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the rate has nothing to do with distinguishing the population eligible to vote in 1997 and the rest of the population. It is a method of taking those born before 1980 who become 18 in 1997 and are illegible to vote. I don't work with rates, aggregate rates produced by statistical authorities because I am using a micro data set, micro level data set. I work with records of information about persons. Every record represents one individual. It is a micro level study. I don't need to use any aggregate level rates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You covered the whole of the population of those who were born before 1980 and you did not study any patterns, representative pattern, nor did you do any calculations. You simply applied the list of those who were born before 1980; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is like extracting records and making a long list of those who became eligible to vote in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you take into account everybody, all persons, or did you extract a sample from the totality of the population?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I explained already 1991 is a complete population survey. If I take from the census all persons born before 1980, then, as a matter of fact, I take one segment of the population which is complete for the ages that it includes, and of course it doesn't contain any other persons that are excluded because of their age. It is not a sample. It is a segment of the population extracted according to the age criterion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you did not need the register of voters. You could simply follow those who existed in 1980; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I would just follow them, then what kind of results could I produce? I had to look at the voters and cross-reference them with this segment of the population reported in the 1991 census in order to be able to study whether they became displaced or not. So my starting point is a segment of the 1991 census, a segment that is related very strictly to the voters of 1997 election, as the voters most certainly can be found in my segment of the 1991 population. It's a longitudinal approach. It is just micro level tracing individuals throughout the time and the sources which report on these individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back to that when we talk about municipalities. I want to go back to Sarajevo for a brief moment. Were you an investigator in the OTP?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't an investigator. The name of my post was demographer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. But were you then an investigator working at the post of an OTP, or rather, were you a researcher?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a post within the OTP, but it wasn't a post of an investigator. I rather think it was a research position called demographer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you obtain your Ph.D. after that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: After, after I was -- I started working at the OTP, no. I obtained my Ph.D. years before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know Mr. Robert Donia and did you collaborate with him?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Donia but we never co-operated. We occasionally met during my work at the OTP at the times he was visiting the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we take Sarajevo as a park, let's use this metaphor, what kind of fluctuation of population would be significant in your view that would warrant the application of the capture/recapture formula? 1.000? 2.000? 10.000?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is not about the fluctuation of the population; it is, you know, about the victims, the number of victims. And when it comes to the reporting of victims in both sources that I used in capture/recapture, there are practically no fluctuations. That is the nature of the sources as such. The thing is that having these two sources I restrict my study to the relevant victim records, victim records that died during the siege period as defined in the Karadzic Sarajevo report or the next one and within the front lines in Sarajevo. So there is no fluctuations here other than that my samples are really samples. I can't be sure that each of these samples is complete. I know they are incomplete. They are just samples.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you take a sample which should represent the whole up to 0.05 per cent margin of error; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- this error margin you mentioned has nothing to do with sample selection, but, you know, the issue you are mentioning, fluctuation of the population, would have been relevant if I studied a different phenomenon, if I studied a disease in a population, and then there would be a migration out and in, there would be birth, then this is relevant fluctuations, of course. But I didn't study diseases, I didn't. I studied a completely different variable, as you said yourself. This is the victim number, that is my variable. And if we speak of a closed population as the one within the front lines in Sarajevo, both sources are not disturbed by any fluctuation. This is the nature of the sources, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Dr. Tabeau, does the number of the fatalities or the casualties can be compared with the number of the population and is it expressed in relative numbers?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. In the Galic report we calculated the rates as well, and for this a complex procedure was used starting with defining what segment of the Sarajevo population covered by household survey Sarajevo was the original as the one who lived there in 1991. And approximately 85 per cent of the population covered by the household survey Sarajevo was the original as in 1991 census. For this we made a pilot study, selected approximately 5.000 questionnaires from a few areas in Sarajevo, questionnaires that were selected disregarding whether or not deaths were reported, just a complete population of 5.000 was picked out. And based on these questionnaires, we studied the distribution of population in Sarajevo household survey. As I said, 85 per cent was original 1991 population; 15 per cent was new population, who this or another way came into Sarajevo and stayed there within the front lines at the time of the survey. Only the original population was taken for the calculation of rates, and only the deaths - I mean the killed people - reported from the original population were taken for the calculation of the rates. So it is just narrowing down the material obtained from Sarajevo household survey, narrowing it down to work with unbiased information and using this information for the calculation of rates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like for us to finish this issue regarding Donia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the number slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting, can we agree that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 21434, 65 ter. This is a book about Sarajevo written by Mr. Donia. Can we have page 3, please. We need the paragraph in the middle that begins with: [In English] "According to ARBiH estimates over a million person-passages were made through the tunnel from July the 30th, 1993, until the end of the war." [Interpretation] And then further on he speaks about the transportation of fuel, food, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that there was such a high frequency of traffic along this tunnel? And if that is true, one can easily say that actually Sarajevo was not under siege at all?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this passage is mentioned, first of all, started in July 30th, 1933 [sic], that is one thing, not in the initial episodes of the siege. And secondly, person-passages, what does it mean actually? Passage? Where did it end? Where did they go when they were leaving the tunnel? So passages just, you know, for me, one way and back perhaps, one and back, one and back. The same person can make thousands of passages this way and back. So it doesn't tell me anything about it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But did you know that the tunnel was so busy that so many persons were going to and fro? It doesn't say exactly, but obviously people travelled in both directions and that tunnel was not part of a closed system; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says, you know, this passage in the book about person-passages, person-passages, not about persons who were leaving the town through the tunnel and moving out from Sarajevo elsewhere. If you go down more to the end lines of the same passage, you know, it tells you what was transferred through the tunnel. So obviously the traffic was two ways. This is how I read it. It was busy, indeed, but on the other hand if the Sarajevo was cut off from the outside world, it is obvious that ways had to be invented for providing aid to the people who lived there. But I don't want to make comments on this because I really didn't study the traffic in the tunnel and who was doing this, how frequently, for what purposes. Obviously there is a description of it in the book of Mr. Donia, and perhaps this can serve as a source on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have these three pages admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I don't have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2249, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come back to Sarajevo. Please, the research that you did, was that a scientific research that was designed in advance in terms of specific procedures and sources to be used in the process?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was scientific research in which decisions were made about sources and methods and procedures, and in the course of this research actually many, many activities were taken to guarantee reliable results of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, it wasn't interpreted. I asked you whether that was a scientific and empirical research or whether that was research conducted on the basis of the data collected from various sources. Did you, yourself, design the scientific and empirical research and did you decide the manner in which the data were to be collected and then you processed them statistically; or were you just given the data collected from various sources?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to stress, nothing is given like that and used like that to produce good, meaningful result. So in order to propose meaningful research, a lot of effort is done to identify right sources and the ways of processing these sources and produce the results. So there was a careful preparation, a very careful preparation of every single report written for this case and other cases. That I used sources compiled by others, like 1991 population census, I can only say I'm extremely happy the census existed, that professional statisticians prepared the census, conducted it and made census files, that I am able to use this census the way I am using it. I am extremely happy that I have the opportunity to use voters' registers in the absence of the next census in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And for the purpose I'm using the voters' register, this source is as good as any other professional statistical source. I am not using voters' register to estimate measures that don't make sense when estimated from this source. I am using it for a certain purpose and for this purpose it is justified to use this source. So I see nothing wrong in using information compiled by others, especially if I make sure that the way of compiling this information is professional and acceptable for research purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not attacking you. Let us just establish the facts. So you believe that a census is a statistical fact. Now, as for the rest, are those statistical facts of the same order like voters' registers and other lists, are they or aren't they?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, census is exceptional among all sources that exist. So voters is of course a different type of source. Well, whether it can be compared with the census, obviously not, because the coverage, the content, the way of making the source is different. But it doesn't mean that we have to disregard the voters' registers as completely useless for our purposes, on the contrary. I can assure you that these are good sources for this type of research as we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, with all due respect, Dr. Tabeau, we are here adding pears and oranges. In your report, you say the reliability is for the most part satisfactory although it cannot be compared to the usual statistical sources. If you made a comparison between the voters' registers from 1996 or 1997, those would be the sources of the similar or identical order. But you had to take the data from 1997 when the Muslims were actually not interested in participating in the elections, and therefore no comparisons can be made, although you did make a reservation here by saying that they cannot be compared with usual statistical sources. Now, this causes concern with me. Why do you say that this is incomparable? Why did you use that term in your report, the term that is now becoming a part of a criminal procedure?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, voters' registers are not comparable with the census, as the methodology of making them is not the same as the one of the census. However, voters' registers are nothing less than a sample of census variables. It is just a sample of basic variables from the census, 1991 census, that the OSCE received from the statistical authority. The variables provided included the names, the date of birth, the place of residence in 1991. That is what was needed for the OSCE to make a voters' register, a voters' register that could be used by the eligible voters to check whether their names are there. And that is what was done in Bosnia in 1997 elections. So voters' register is different from the census. Census reports on many more variables than just the three I mentioned. It reports about ethnicity. It reports about religion. It reports about the education, marital status, children. It reports about place of birth, about the place of residence, about the profession, about the employment, about the housing, about the agricultural farms. It's huge. It is unique. That is the census. We don't have all these variables in the voters' register. Voters' register is a simple register with names, JMBG, date of birth, place of residence, not good enough to make a statistical study of the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1997, by all means not good enough to take it as a list of registered voters who can be compared with the census records and studied from the point of view of their displacement. These are the differences between these sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I am currently disregarding different variables that the register does not comprise. What I'm primarily interested in is the number. Do you know that in our country people have to be registered again and again for each election and that in many cases people simply don't register themselves and don't feature in the voters' registers?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what is the question, but if it is whether the voters' register is incomplete then the answer is yes, it is incomplete. Only those who registered are there in the register.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just finish the previous question. Was there any difference between what you did and the data that you obtained or obtained by other sources for various purposes and is it different from research that you set up in advance in terms of standards and procedures that would govern the collection of data and after that you proceeded with the collection of data? Would that constitute two different ways of research and which would be your preference between the two? Would you prefer to have standards set up in advance? In other words, that would be a longitudinal research that would produce the data collected on the basis of your design.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to keep it short, the question is whether there exists something like a perfect research design and how far I ended from this perfect design. Well, when it comes to the study of displacements, ideally I would like to use the second census, post-war census. However, I don't have it and even today I don't have it. What I selected, the voters' register, is an excellent replacement of what is unavailable. So the other alternative that exists is not to do anything at all. I believe that what has been done with the voters' register and the 1991 population census is of high scientific standard and is reliable. Moreover, there are sources that can be compared, independent sources, and results can be confronted. I did such a comparison and I can tell that this study based on voters' register does not significantly differ from the official registration by UNHCR of displaced persons and refugees. When it comes to victims, ideally we would all like to see a complete list of all victims with all kind of details and the name of the perpetrator next to each victim. That is the ideal that we are all looking for. This ideal doesn't exist. It's very challenging to produce a list that could be covering a part of this ideal, a pattern that can be produced based on existing sources. I believe that in all these studies, Sarajevo studies, and in Srebrenica we have come very close to this ideal in terms of numbers, not in terms of perpetrators. This has never been the subject of my report. But in terms of numbers, I think we are very close and sources that we used are also highly reliable and meaningful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why was then this study performed based on other sources if you say that you had official registrations made by the UNHCR? Were there any flaws in that UNHCR registration that led to it not being applied in this instance?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think UNHCR can themselves testify about what they have done. So the whole point of this study we made is to make an independent study based on good sources and compare the results with the work of UNHCR. So that's the essence of this work. We work with primary sources, we work with names, we have applied a careful approach I think a good methodology, and this is why it is worthwhile to do this kind of work and to present results as completely independent to what UNHCR has been doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that the Defence should understand this to mean that the OTP and their services are more objective in their approach to this problem than the UNHCR?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I am an expert for the Prosecutor -- for the Prosecution, but in my opinion I am working to provide the true picture of what happened. And I have been doing this the best way I can by studying always all ethnicities, complete areas, complete time episodes. I work with many sources. I cross-reference the sources. I confront the sources with each other in order to present as independent picture as possible. I don't consider myself working for the Prosecution or for anybody else. I am -- my role is to provide an independent opinion on what happened. It happened that I was part of the OTP 11 years long; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Maybe we shall -- back to this issue later on. Let me ask you this: There is no dispute between us that the bureau of statistics is fully qualified and competent to carry out census. Now, as for the sources who collected the data that you used, are these sources -- have equally valid credentials? Are they certified?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly what you mean, "certified," credentials. I used the ICRC list of missing persons, ICMP list of identifications, Sarajevo household survey. I think these are -- yeah, international organisations, very well-known, and who operating -- has been operating for very long time, especially ICRC, and I believe this is the best credentials as I can have for these sources. Yeah, I also use Sarajevo household survey, a survey that was conducted by a local -- by group of local researchers in Sarajevo. And I actually checked the questionnaire they developed and the procedures they used for completing the survey, but the computerisation of these questionnaires and data processing, cleaning of the data, everything was done here by my unit and others who were involved in projects with me. So even though the questionnaire was developed down there, in Sarajevo, first I see this is a good questionnaire; second, I received the original questionnaires for my processing, I arrange everything myself according to good standards. So I don't think we have a problem here as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I wasn't clear enough. I am not dealing with Sarajevo only. I'm asking you in principle. For instance, if, for example, a music society were to come up and give you their information and when we use the word "music society" or singing society, that means that there's nothing binding involved. For example, who is this, PIP, the Podrinje Identification Project, are they certified for working on statistical methods? Are they competent? Are they objective? And has that been confirmed anywhere?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Podrinje Identification Project that you mentioned is not a source I used. It is just an organisation down there, in Bosnia, who works together with ICMP on the identification of victims. What matters for me is the ICMP itself, International Commission For Missing Persons, who are certified, I am sure, and there was probably another person from ICMP to tell about the certificates they have. But for me what mattered, I had the occasion to visit ICMP several times in the course of my work at the OTP. I had the opportunity to check personally how they work, what kind of procedures are in place. For the whole process from, you know, taking samples from the remains, sending them to the lab, DNA profiling, you know, putting into the database, the same with the blood samples of the relatives, how the matching is done, how the coding is done, how the storage is done. So I could have assessed this for myself, and that is, in my view, the best certificate in my eyes, you know, about the reliability of this source. But of course the methodology ICMP uses is a worldwide standard, so it is not that they invented the method of DNA profiling and matching; they just use the methodology. And I use the results of the matching.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I was not referring to the ICMP, although I think that at that time even the ICMP hadn't had an international licence. However, we had their witnesses here as well. This is what I'm interested in, though, that is the extent to which you relied on sources. Now let us look at something else. As far as municipalities are concerned, you did some research on demographic trends in relation to the consequences of war, or rather, causes and consequences of war in 27 municipalities and then especially within that context in nine municipalities. Do you know how many municipalities exist in Republika Srpska or do you accept, rather, that there are 62 of them?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the exact numbers, but if you are telling me 62, I accept this number. I will check it, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So is it the task of the Prosecution or was it the task of the Prosecution - and within that context your task as well - to provide evidence on lawful or unlawful action taken by the Serb side - and myself in particular - in relation to a certain area?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I said earlier in my testimony that I didn't study causes of migration, and of course I didn't study all lawful or unlawful actions of yourself or anybody else. It is not part of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But this is what I'm interested in now. What do these 27 municipalities mean? Are they a sample for all of Republika Srpska? Or even more, for the entire area that we had under our control during the war?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 27 municipalities were selected according to the indictment of this case. This is initially as it was presented at some point, at the time the report was made. So it is not a sample. It is just the area covered by the indictment of the case, Karadzic case, that is studied in our municipalities report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you expressed all results in relative terms as well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As percentages, you mean. That the change in the ethnic composition was expressed in percentages. But still, you know, I used both absolute terms and relative terms in relation to the 27 municipalities selected in accordance to the indictment of the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since you're a statistician and a demographer, would you have had a different result if you added to the 27 municipalities a 28th one, for instance, Gradiska and as a 29th one Srbac, and as a 30th one Derventa, say all of those municipalities, then the entire autonomous region of the Krajina that had 18 or more municipalities itself. What would the result be given that sample, or, rather, given this mass that would be looked at statistically?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the numbers that I present relate to the 27 municipalities. If I change this number, if I add new municipalities, the numbers must change obviously because the calculation will be done for a new area that is different from the 27 municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Out of these 27 municipalities, if we were to take nine municipalities where the fiercest fighting took place and where the denouement was the most dramatic then these results become even more dense, isn't that right, I mean they're even more convincing as claimed by the indictment?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it doesn't work like this. You know, if we ask the question how many persons became displaced from the area of 27 municipalities versus nine out of 27, so that obviously for nine municipalities the number will be smaller than for 27. That is as simple as that. Ethnic composition might be then showing more dramatic changes for the nine municipalities, of course. If these were -- municipalities were -- these events, as you call them were dense. But it is not that we were making a selection in our report. We make a report consistent with the indictment area, and there is no manipulation here with the number of municipalities. The indictment says 27 municipalities. We take 27 and make an analysis for the 27. And the other day last week there was a mention that seven have been dropped out of 27, so it would be good to see the picture for the 20 municipalities instead. That is how it works. What comes out is just the result of the analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up in e-court chapter 3 are the main findings. They have to do with Croats -- actually, it's all the same to me. Any map of these municipalities, say number 5 from this chapter. I'm calling this up not because of the Croats but because of the image itself. For instance, we can also have number 7 from chapter 4. Any one of them. We just need to see the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are certainly informed that I was president in all of Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P4994, page 5 within this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that I was president - I mean that I was president - in all of these municipalities, even in those that in Dayton we handed over to the Federation; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the coloured one enlarged. We don't really need the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Tabeau, since I have been accused of systematic persecution, a system that was applied in Republika Srpska, do you believe -- for example, look at the west, Dubica, it is north of Prijedor, 009; then Gradiska, also to the north of Prijedor; then Prnjavor, then Srbac, these are just four municipalities closer to the Sava River up there. Had you included them, what would this system of persecution look like percentage-wise?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that, but if you want and you ask me then I can recalculate some statistics for you for the entire Republika Srpska. But I don't think that entire Republika Srpska is part of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But if it's a system that is involved, if I have been accused of systematic behaviour based on a system, does it not mean that in some municipalities they did listen to me and in others they did not? And did they obey me in the municipalities where there hadn't been any persecution, or did they obey me in the municipalities where there hadn't been any persecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for the witness to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I just want to comment on the figures for Republika Srpska. They are available from the report, municipalities report. On page 66, for example, in table 2BH, there is an overview of the minimum number of displaced persons for the entire country Bosnia and Herzegovina with the division into Republika Srpska and the Federation. And there is a similar table for the estimated number of displaced persons and refugees which is next page, 67, and there is the change in the ethnic composition on page 65. So pages 65, 66, 67 contain these statistics. So I'm not hiding anything. Whatever I have, I present in this report. So there is a context for the figures for 27 municipalities in terms of the figures for Republika Srpska as a whole. Well, I don't think the picture is so dramatically different really. The numbers of displaced persons are larger, though, and very much so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you certainly do not deal with displaced persons only. You also deal with the density of the events concerned, and if we look at the framework involved it is of crucial importance to look at things in their entirety. One of the key values involved is the total area because it is expressed in real terms.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say it's all there, it's all there, the 27 municipalities, the entire Republika Srpska, it's all there in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that establishing the density of events in nine municipalities in 27 municipalities is insignificant from the point of view of this criminal case and from the point of view of the indictment for the purposes of which you worked? Is the density of the developments concerned of significance?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly what do you mean by "density," in terms of relative measures certain percentages are presented in the municipalities report. That's the only relative measure that is discussed there. So I think this is the density, I guess, you referred to. And if I have to answer whether it is right to show these densities, meaning the fractions of displaced persons in various configurations, the answer is, yes, it is 100 per cent correct to calculate such percentages for every municipality in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the entire area of political entities, Republika Srpska and Federation, and for any other area composed of selected municipalities. It all depends what is -- why these statistics are needed. In this case, the calculation is presented for 27 municipalities because this is how the indictment area was defined. If the area would be larger, like the entire Republika Srpska, we would be including consequences that are not necessarily -- that would be not covered by the indictment, which would be completely unjustified then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please focus on chapter 2 of your report with the annex for this case, the main findings that pertain to Muslims, so I'm looking at 2.1. And you say in 27 municipalities included in the indictment the share of Muslims decreased from 41 per cent, as it was in 1991, to 32.8 per cent in 1997, or, rather, the decrease was 19.9 per cent. First of all, do we agree that the share of Muslims in the general population does not depend only on trends involving the Muslims but also on trends involving others, the arrival of Serbs in this area, does it decrease the percentage of Muslims that are there?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is e-court page 9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Now to the question about the trend. Well, there is no trend in my report. There is this one 1991 population as reported in the census and ethnicity is reported as of the moment of the census, and it is from -- coming from an open-ended question, so everybody tells what he or she thinks he or she is, end of story. There is no trend. So the ethnic composition is calculated on this given moment of time. And the same is done again for 1997. The whole point is about, you know, movements of the population, that certain groups moved out, certain other groups moved in in a given territory. So if the ethnic composition is shown on two different moments of time, then there is a change, a change which has nothing to do with any trend in a report being of ethnic or anything like that because still the same definition of ethnicity is used. It is just the two -- these two ethnic compositions summarise the change that took place between the two moments of time. And if one group is gone and replaced by another group, this will be seen in the change of the ethnic composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, if one group hadn't left and the other group increased its numbers, does that affect the structure?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course this will be reflected in the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So 41 per cent and 32.8 per cent is the share of the Muslims in the general population in these 27 municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then taking into account all the things that can affect this, including Serbs moving in, for instance, we cannot just take it for granted that 19.9 per cent Muslims left; rather, perhaps more Serbs moved in. Right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the beauty of this report is said that you have numbers of the population movement for every ethnic group. So these are the displacements, for Muslims, and Serbs, Croats, others. So on one hand there is this change in the ethnic composition, but on the other hand you just go to figures related to the displacement which are discussed in paragraph 2.2 and 2.3 in the same section.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: So for my ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that, Ms. Tabeau. We'll get to that. So does this mean the following: That in these 27 municipalities in 1997 there were 67.2 per cent non-Muslims, that is to say Serbs and Croats, if we're only looking at point 2.1?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you calculate the 19.9 per cent, on the basis of absolute numbers or did you subtract 32.8 from 41 per cent and then did you calculate the percentages of percentages?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the relative difference, this is how it is called in statistics, it's the difference between 41 per cent and 32.8 per cent divided by 41 per cent. It is a relative difference, a relative difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it -- wouldn't it be more accurate to use absolute numbers and then to base the percentage on the difference in absolute numbers?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we don't do this with absolute numbers because for 1997 it is a large sample but a sample. So if we look at the absolute numbers, this could be misleading. Some people could take the absolute numbers as the size of the population in 1997, which is not true. It is just a sample. So it is much more correct to work with just percentages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But please take a look at this. 41 per cent and 32.8 per cent are percentages that have to do with the general population, whereas 19.9 per cent are percentages within the Muslim community itself; right?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is a change in the fraction of Muslims between 1991 and 1997. That change expressed as a percentage, it is almost a 20 per cent decline, almost 20 per cent. That's it. I -- what is the problem here? I really don't understand. It would be of course easier to look at 1.000 versus 2.000 or 10.000 versus 50.000. Of course it would be, but we don't have complete numbers for the 1997 population so we have to live with percentages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, I'm trying to say the following: When Serbs move into Serb areas, that could also change the share of Muslims in the general population; right? And we cannot say there are less Muslims in the general population by 19.9 per cent?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 19.9 per cent is the change in the ethnic composition, in the fraction of Muslims, in the fraction of Muslims in 1997 as compared with 1991. And in terms of absolute numbers, we don't know how many Muslims left in 1997 in these 27 municipalities. We can only tell a minimum number of Muslims living in these 27 municipalities. That's all we can tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it's time to adjourn for today, but before doing so just shall we do the calculation here. Doctor, 41.0 minus 32.8 is 8.2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That should be exactly 20 per cent, why 19.9 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I have to recalculate if it is not exactly as Your Honour thinks it should be, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May I just quickly do some corrections to the transcript, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Page 60, line 12, there are two times where the witness said DEM-2, D-E-M-2. On the transcript, it's too, t-o-o. Page 62, line 3, there is a blank. It should be JMBG, J-M-B-G. Page 63, line 24, the words should be "deficient," not "definition." Page 55, line 2, it should be "counts of victims," not "kinds of victims." And then page 77, the witness was talking about that the voter registration was not good enough to make a study in 1997, but in line 20 she said by all means good enough to take it as a list of registered of voters, if there's any disagreement on here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. West. We continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of May, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.
